heading: ### Tested hypothesis and bounded result
lead: **Question refined this cycle:** Can an attention SC_SZC slot keep all folded tables on a device while leaving the exact CFS masking and Fiat–Shamir schedule on the host, and when would round trips erase the benefit? The baseline is current CPU generic `hashline/src/zk.rs::masked_prove` -> `zkp-core/src/sumcheck.rs::prove`. Candidate: upload once, compute/reduce one unmasked round vector on device, mask/absorb/draw on host, return challenge, fold all tables on device. It moves CPU table scanning but **eliminates zero table reads or field operations** in the source schedule. It adds upload, final transfer, 2–3 launches and one dependent host/device exchange per round, VRAM residency and integration cost. No mask, salt or private-opening reuse is proposed.  [One-thread experiment](experiments/sc-szc-device-round-20260927/README.md): seed 2026092713; four synthetic SC_SZC-shaped profiles with 8–128 rows, 13/26 Fp2 tables, degree four and tiles of 3/7/16 pairs. In 0.510 s/17,140 KiB RSS on Intel Core Ultra 9 185H, 110 round samples match an independently reconstructed original Boolean-cube MLE oracle; 91 finals, masked claim chain and eight negative controls pass. At 128 rows/26 tables, tiles 16 and 3 have identical complete masked-message digests. The source CFS formula is transcribed; the polynomial is a simplified three-group stand-in, and the challenge hash is a test SHA-256, **not** Rust BLAKE3. No native/GPU receipt parity or speed result. Source/script SHA-256, command, dimensions and limits are in `result.json`.
tail: At synthetic N=128/k=26/d=4, once-only upload is 53,248 B; source-counted table round/fold reads 211,328 B and writes 52,832 B in **both** CPU-style and device-resident schedules. Reduced vectors total 560 B D2H, seven challenges 112 B H2D, finals 416 B. At least seven sequential challenge exchanges survive; a separate device reduction adds seven launches. Sending tile partials instead costs 880/3,680 B at tile 16/3. These are logical counts, not DRAM/time. The device route is useful only if measured GPU execution beats CPU work after transfers/synchronization. As a generous ceiling, deleting the entire *approximate* 8.565 s softmax slot at zero cost from the 30.055 s one-block wall leaves ~21.49 s, a ~28.5% wall reduction. This candidate can remove less. The complete private 8B ceiling and >=50 tokens/s feasibility are unknown. Falsify on byte/terminal/refusal mismatch, VRAM overflow, or no quiesced enclosing proof gain. [Handoff](handoffs/20260927-sc-szc-device-round.md) names the patch seam and validation.
